Anya: Heads-up — while validating the Mixtral-8x AWQ profile on prod-like workloads we saw a ~1.8x tail latency regression for long sequences (seq=1024) compared to the GPTQ profile. KV cache hit rates dropped and the runtime fell back to a slower attention kernel in a bunch of traces.

Ryan: Can you paste the profiler excerpt?

Anya: Sure — here's a trimmed profiler for the problematic run: 
```
PROFILE summary: model=mixtral-8x-awq env=dedicated-gpu-3
seq_len=1024 batch_size=6 tokens_generated=12k
kernel:attn_fused   avg=12.4ms p95=24.1ms (used when qkv_dim % 32 == 0)
kernel:attn_unfused avg=19.8ms p95=38.6ms (fallback path)
kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.58 -> effective_tokens/sec=3.9k
cache_misses_correlated_with_prefix_change=true
notes: per-request routing decided AWQ variant due to cost_policy=low
```

Santiago: Hmm — that fallback to attn_unfused rings a bell. Mixtral's head/kvdims are non-standard (heads=32, kv_dim=96 -> 3072 total per-head layout) which trips our fused kernel alignment checks. When RoPE scaling !=1.0 we also do a different rotary pipeline which currently disables a few fused optimizations.

Mia: tl;dr: mismatch in heads/kv dims + RoPE scale path -> fused kernel not selected -> slower. Also batching is making warm cache less likely because we mix many prefix lengths.

Ryan: Two immediate ideas: (1) loosen fused-kernel alignment rule for Mixtral family when quantized with AWQ, with a guard that checks numerical accuracy (small test). (2) change batching heuristic to coalesce by prefix-length bucket to increase KV cache reuse.

Anya: I ran a quick micro A/B last night. With the proposed kernel override we get ~1.35x reduction in median per-token latency on the same trace but we need to check accuracy/regression metrics.

Santiago: Accuracy numbers I pulled from the eval run: AWQ (current calibrations) vs GPTQ on Qwen-7B / Mixtral-8x: 
- Qwen-7B AWQ int8: +0.2% exact-match on short QA, -0.9% on the long-context LM score
- Mixtral-8x AWQ int8: -0.6% LM score, GPTQ int8: -0.2%
So AWQ is cheaper and often faster but more sensitive to certain RoPE/scaling interactions.

Alex: For calibration we should standardize on a 256-token calibration prompt set sampled from the eval holdout across genres (QA, code, dialog). Using 256 instead of 128 captures more RoPE-phase diversity. Also try FP8 mixed calibration for a smaller drop with better perf.

Mia: On batching heuristics — propose we add 2 buckets: short-prefix (<=64) and long-prefix (>64). Route incoming requests into in-flight batches by bucket, with a soft timeout of 6ms to avoid tail latency blowups. This should increase same-prefix batching and boost kv_cache_hit_ratio.

Anya: Agreed. Also add an instrumentation tag: `kernel_fallback_reason` with values like `rope_scale_mismatch`, `qkv_alignment`, `quant_backend_incompat`. We need this telemetry before enabling the kernel override so we can measure correctness & stability.

Ryan: For rollout plan — canary the kernel override + batching change on the dedicated cluster (low-cost tier) for 48 hours, compare p50/p95 and eval suites. If AWQ accuracy drops >0.8% on long-LM metrics, rollback.

Santiago: I'll prepare the extended calibration runs: AWQ int8, GPTQ int8, AWQ+FP8 mixed. Use 256 token calibration prompts, sample=1k prompts. I'll push the artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/mixtral/calib/175300.

Alex: I'll run the accuracy regression harness against the canary traces and post diffs.

Mia: I'll prototype the prefix bucketing change in the async-batcher and add the `kernel_fallback_reason` tag in the runtime. Patch incoming later today.

Anya: Cool. Action items: (1) Santiago run calibs and upload artifacts (2) Mia add batching + telemetry PR (3) Ryan coordinate canary (4) Alex run accuracy diffs. We will reconvene after 48h.

ops-bot: Scheduled canary deploy: dedicated-gpu-3 cluster -> kernel-override + batching-v2 at 2025-11-02T03:00:00Z (UTC). Canary window=48h. Assigned: @Ryan, @Mia.

Ryan: thanks — tagging this as high-priority. Will monitor dashboards and the new `kernel_fallback_reason` tag. :eyes:

Santiago: one more note — if RoPE scaling is the root cause we might need a small change in our rotary implementation to keep fused paths enabled. I'll try a prototype that preserves the fused codegen semantics for non-unit RoPE.

Anya: Nice. If that works we can avoid the override and keep correctness-first. Either way, prioritized for this sprint. :tada:
